outcome.answer: Yes—several of these papers use graph-based representations or graph-oriented models for chemical reaction prediction and optimization. RxnCLF builds a condensed reaction graph that unifies reactant and product information into a single graph to learn transformation-aware reaction representations for reactivity/yield prediction [1]. For broader chemical reaction informatics, dynamic reaction-condition representations are learned by encoding textual reaction conditions with a fine-tuned language model inside a multi-objective Bayesian optimization loop [8].
